newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr stays strong vs yen by late Tokyo but off high.
newsitem.headline: Dlr stays strong vs yen by late Tokyo but off high.

text.p: 0646 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar stayed strong against the yen in late Tokyo on Tuesday after paring earlier losses on long liquidation sales in afternoon trade, dealers said.

"Dealers started unwinding their long positions after confirming that the dollar's topside is heavy near 116.70 yen," a dealer at a long-term credit bank said. The dollar rose as high as 116.69 yen by late Tokyo.
Amid market holidays in London and New York, the dollar climbed as high as 116.72 yen in Toronto on Monday on purchases by U.S. investment houses, dealers said.
Dealers said the dollar came off earlier highs partly due to a sharp rise in Japaneses market interst rates.
The benchmark 182nd Japanese government bond yield rose briefly by 0.1 percentage percent from the previous day's close to 2.680 percent in the afternoon.
But dealers said buying interest, possibly by Japanese investors near and below 116 yen, kept the greenback's downside solid.

In crosses, market talk that a Japanese television station reported that new British trade chief Margaret Beckett said there was a possibility Britain would rejoin the ERM sparked selling of sterling for the mark and yen, dealers said.

Sterling fell as low as around 189.46 yen in reaction to the talk, but dealers said later the talk was proved groundless. The British currency stood at 190.10/22 yen at 0702 GMT against 190.77 yen in early Tokyo trading.
Sterling sales indirectly pushed the dollar/yen rate down amid lack of fresh and significant factors in dollar/yen trade alone, but dealers said the impact was short-lived.

Beckett said in a speech to the British Chamber of Commerce in Tokyo that the Labour government would not be indecisive about whether to join a single European currency, but she did not give a hint of what Labour's decision would be on European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Dealers said they are closely watching moves by overseas traders to see how they react to the unexpected poll result in France on Sunday after market holidays in London and New York on Monday. "We did not have many market-moving factors in dollar/yen trade, so now we are focusing on moves by overseas traders on their entry in European trade," a bank dealer said.

Some dealers said U.S. operators were keen to sell marks for yen in afternoon trade. A Japanese bank dealer in Singapore said there were stop-loss buying orders around 69.20/25 in mark/yen trade and traders had gone long in the morning but failed to hit the stops.

The mark stood at around 68.52/55 yen at 0731 GMT, compared with 69.14 yen in early Tokyo trading. A long-term credit bank dealer said dollar/mark trade remained directionless for most of the Asian session.
